summary: A round-trip search must support independent outbound and return departure-time windows across every search path, while preserving the outbound window as the return fallback when no independent window is set.
reason: Google Flights' own RPC and fallback page both support per-leg time restrictions, but flight-goat's request builder (buildOneSegment) and the HTML-fallback bucket parser (flightsFromEmbeddedPayload, outbound at inner[2] / inbound at inner[3]) only ever forwarded one shared TimeWindow to both legs. Round-trip users commonly want different windows per direction (e.g. don't leave before noon outbound, don't return before evening) and had no way to express that.
validated_outcome: go build ./... ; go vet ./... ; go test ./... all pass, including new tests TestBuildOfferSegments_ReturnTimeWindowAppliesToInboundOnly, TestBuildOfferSegments_ReturnTimeWindowFallsBackToTimeWindow, TestFlightsFromEmbeddedPayload_OutboundReturnSplit, and TestFilterFlightsClientSide_ReturnTimeWindowAppliesOnlyToReturnBucket. python3 .github/scripts/verify-skill/verify_skill.py --dir library/travel/flight-goat/ passes. govulncheck ./... reports 0 reachable vulnerabilities.
